passages.note: Senate concurrence/final passage vote on 2SB 100 School Gender Identity Policies; Cullimore voted Yea, 6 of 29 against so not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: without written parental consent make changes to a student's education record
passages.note: Operative section guarantees parental access to education records and requires parental consent for gender-identity changes to the record; it neither mandates proactive notification (rung 4) nor requires permission before staff use a name or pronouns (rung 5), and goes beyond on-request access (rung 3).

rows.reasoning: Cullimore voted Yea on SB 100 (2023), which bars schools from shielding a student's education record from parents and forbids changing the record's gender identity "without written parental consent". That places him on the parental-involvement side, but the bill's object is the education record, not staff use of names or pronouns ("Require parental permission before staff use a different name or pronouns") nor a duty to notify parents ("Require schools to notify parents"), so no single rung's clauses are fully matched.
